calls.prompt:
Company: Ledgerly Inc.

US mid-size fintech (~600 employees). Licensed money transmitter in 48 states. Consumer app offering P2P payments, debit card (issued via a partner bank), cross-border remittances to 30 countries, and a custodial crypto wallet (buy/sell/send BTC, ETH, USDC). Small-business invoicing. No lending, no securities brokerage, not a bank.

Rules that APPLY:
- Bank Secrecy Act / AML, FinCEN rules for MSBs, Travel Rule, CVC rules
- OFAC sanctions screening (customers and counterparties, incl. crypto addresses)
- CFPB rules: Reg E (EFTA), remittance rule, prepaid rule, UDAAP, larger-participant rules for payment apps
- Consumer data privacy / GLBA, open banking (1033)
- FTC consumer protection that touches payment apps
- Stablecoin / digital asset regulation affecting custodial wallets

Rules that DO NOT apply:
- SEC rules for exchanges, broker-dealers, investment companies, SRO rule filings
- Bank capital rules, bank holding company filings, deposit insurance assessments
- CFTC derivatives market rules (DCMs, swaps)
- Tax rules unless they create information reporting for payment platforms or digital assets
- Sanctions actions only matter via the screening program, not individually

Affected areas and owners:
- aml-bsa: AML/BSA program, FinCEN, Travel Rule, SARs → Priya Shah (BSA Officer)
- sanctions: OFAC screening and sanctions compliance → Marcus Lee (Sanctions)
- consumer-payments: Reg E, remittances, prepaid, CFPB supervision, UDAAP → Dana Ortiz (Consumer Compliance)
- crypto: Custodial wallet, stablecoins, CVC-specific rules → Sam Okafor (Digital Assets Counsel)
- privacy: Privacy, data security, open banking / 1033 → Lena Novak (Privacy)
- tax: Information reporting (1099-K, 1099-DA) → Ravi Menon (Tax)

Task: Find every US Federal Register document published between 2026-11-09 and 2026-11-13 (inclusive) that affects this company. For each, give the Federal Register document number, title, federalregister.gov URL, the key deadline, a tier (Critical if a deadline is < 90 days from 2026-11-13, otherwise High/Medium/Low by importance), the owner area, a one-line reason, and a one-line action. Only include items you found via search. Return an empty list if none.

items.title: Imposition of Special Measure Prohibiting the Transmittal of Funds Involving MEXC Global
items.reason: FinCEN found MEXC Global, a foreign CVC exchanger, to be of primary money laundering concern. The order bars covered financial institutions from transmitting funds to or from it, and Ledgerly's custodial wallet sends and receives crypto. It takes effect 12/10/2026, which is under 90 days away.
items.action: Before 12/10/2026, add MEXC Global entities and known addresses to wallet and counterparty screening. Set up a reject-and-report workflow for inbound CVC transfers from MEXC. Block outbound sends to MEXC. Coordinate with Sanctions (Marcus Lee) and Digital Assets (Sam Okafor).

items.title: Threshold for the Requirement To Collect, Retain, and Transmit Information on Funds Transfers and Transmittals of Funds That Begin or End Outside the United States, and Clarification of the Requirement To Collect, Retain, and Transmit Information on Transactions Involving Convertible Virtual Currencies and Digital Assets With Legal Tender Status; Withdrawal
items.reason: FinCEN and the Federal Reserve withdrew the 2020 proposal to cut the Recordkeeping/Travel Rule threshold from $3,000 to $250 for cross-border transfers. The same proposal would have expressly extended the rules to CVC. The withdrawal means Ledgerly's remittance and crypto Travel Rule thresholds stay at $3,000, with no new obligation.
items.action: Record the withdrawal in the Travel Rule regulatory tracker. Confirm the $3,000 threshold in Travel Rule procedures and the remittance and crypto transfer-monitoring logic. Drop any planning for a $250 threshold.
